verdict.rationale: Solid's own README says its minimal abstractions give direct access to the DOM, so native libraries like D3 are easy to use. It compiles templates to real DOM nodes, and a hands-on user confirms that refs are just the elements. Another user relies on Solid for data viz. missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs on the integration pattern (refs and lifecycle hooks for mounting or cleaning up third-party libraries), and a hands-on report of integrating a specific charting library such as D3.

support.subject: As a developer, I can directly manipulate the DOM to integrate existing browser libraries like charting or visualization tools

citations.quote: Solid's bare-metal, minimal abstractions give you direct access to the DOM, making it easy to use your favorite native JavaScript libraries like D3.
Instead of using a Virtual DOM, it compiles its templates to real DOM nodes and updates them with fine-grained reactions.
